content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether to use relative imports matching repo convention versus the "agentic-3js-builder" module path mentioned in the prompt, since there's no src/index.ts to resolve that import for typechecking purposes.

My plan is to write with relative imports first to typecheck locally, then swap them to the single module path via a find-and-replace afterward. I'm mapping out which exports live where: builder, frame, math helpers, path utilities, ik, paint, texture, and the glow kit submodule.

Now I'm designing the elephant's proportions at realistic scale, roughly 3.3m shoulder height and 6m total length, facing +Z, and sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting from hips as root through a spine chain connecting pelvis, chest, shoulder, and neck base.

Working through the spine curve points from rump to head base, calibrating body loft stations (center height, width, height) at various z positions along the torso so the belly clearance and shoulder peak land near realistic elephant measurements like a ~1.3m belly height and ~3.3m shoulder top.

Now I'm setting up the skeleton structure: a spine bone chain, a tail chain off the rump, and a large skull-sized head with the trunk hanging down and curling toward the ground. For the skin, I'm planning a gray-brown base color with layered painting effects — a reddish-brown dust tint on the lower body to mimic mud, plus wrinkle lines generated procedurally with sine-based noise bands.

Writing wrinkle/trunk paint functions...

Now I'm defining the skeleton hierarchy, starting with a hips root joint and building the spine chain forward from it with positioned bones for skinning the body loft.

The tail continues curving back and downward from the rump into four segments, parented to hips. Since the body loft runs from the rear station through the spine, I'm figuring out how the rear portion behind hips should project onto the hips joint as a single bone segment rather than a chain.

I'll just try assigning it to [spine, hips] and verify by running the preview rather than overthinking the projection logic.

Now I'm positioning the head and neck: a short thick neck chain of two joints connecting the spine's end near (0,2.35,1.85) up to the head base around (0,2.65,2.15), with the head joint itself placed forward at roughly (0,2.7,1.95) to sit in front of the shoulders like an elephant's skull. I'm extending the spine to four joints feeding into this neck chain, then building the skull as a scaled sphere.

Modeling the lower jaw as a small wedge beneath the head, positioned under where the trunk attaches, and then laying out a six-joint trunk chain running from the skull front down near the ground with a curled tip.

Adding ridge rings using thin torus shapes aligned to the trunk sweep's tangent direction, scaled to match the trunk radius at each point...

For the trunk tip I'm adding two small finger-like capsule bumps plus dark nostril circles, mimicking an African elephant's dual-lobed trunk tip. Now I'm working out the tusk geometry—curved ivory shapes starting near the cheek, dipping down then sweeping forward and up, sized around 1.5m for an adult.

I'm defining the tusk sweep as a cubic bezier with tapering radius and an ivory gradient (brownish tip, paler base), placed rigidly on the head with a pinkish-gray collar ring at the base and darker wear marks near the tip, positioned clear of the trunk. Next I'm turning to the ears—large fan-shaped extruded plates roughly 1.2m tall to capture that big leaf-like African elephant silhouette.

Working out ear plate geometry and orientation vectors...

Mapping out the ear's outline points to extend down to a drooping pointed tip, then setting thickness and bevel so it sits naturally against the shoulder.

Now I'm adding inner-ear detail with a paint function for pinkish mottled texture and radiating vein lines based on angle from the root, plus thinking about whether a rim edge needs a second slightly larger plate or just a tapered thickness profile.

For the ears, I'm setting up the bone joint positioned near the top of the skull with a direction for aiming, plus adding a capsule base where the ear meets the head. Then I'm positioning the eyes on the side of the skull sphere using a surface-around helper with azimuth and elevation angles to place them correctly relative to the trunk and forward direction.

For the eye detail itself, I'm planning a decal with an SVG-drawn eye showing amber iris, dark pupil, white highlight, and wrinkled lid, plus a wrinkle brow ridge wedge above it. Then I'm laying out the four legs as pillar-like columns, defining shoulder and foot coordinates for front and hind legs with elephants' characteristic near-straight posture, though the hind legs need slightly more bend.

Working out leg segment lengths so the knees bend forward just enough to look natural while keeping the reach close to the actual joint distances, then naming the joint chains like shoulder/elbow/wrist for front legs and hip/knee/ankle for hind legs.

I'm sizing the sweep radii along each leg so they taper from thick near the body to narrower at the ankle before flaring out into the foot pad, and shaping the foot as a short rounded cylinder with a few toenail bumps on the front edge.

Still shaping nail geometry...

Now I'm working out the leg skeleton: hip joint down through a knee to the ankle target near the ground, treating it as a two-segment limb chain ending at the foot.

I'm setting foot cylinder dimensions so the leg tube caps neatly into the sole, with radius tapering from thigh (0.5) down to ankle (0.31) across five keyframes along the chain. I'm also planning wrinkle texture bands down the leg and considering adding sphere bulges at the hips for thigh volume.

Now I'm thinking through the tail — a thin tapered sweep with a bristly dark tuft of spikes at the tip, built as a four-joint chain with thick wrinkle detail, plus a few sparse bristle hair cards scattered on the head and back using a hair texture to mimic elephant bristles.

I'm also planning skin fold details like wrinkle creases at leg and knee joints, and figuring out the lower jaw — a separate part hinged near the head joint beneath the trunk base, roughly shaped as a flattened sphere or capsule to suggest the jawline and lips.

Rather than using a single sphere for the skull, I think a loft is better: I'm laying out head stations from back of skull to forehead, each with its own width and height, narrowing toward the front where the trunk attaches, then overlapping that with the body loft's front stations so the head and body blend smoothly at the neck.

For the chain structure, I'll keep spine and neck as separate chains with a few joints each, feeding into the head joint, and simplify naming so hips sit at the root with a defined starting position.

Since hips sits at the same point as spine1, I'll treat it as a zero-length bone and exclude it from the body loft list, keeping just spine and neck for that path. The tail chain attaches to hips starting slightly behind it, and I'm figuring out whether hind and front legs should parent off hips or spine1.

Now I'm narrowing down leg placement relative to body width—legs at x=±0.7 with 0.4 radius slightly overshoot the body's half-width, so I'm adjusting them inward to around x=±0.62. I'm sketching out the body loft stations from tail to shoulder with position, width, and height values to get a realistic elephant silhouette.

Checking the top height at shoulder works out to around 3.4m, a bit tall but plausible for a big bull, and belly clearance of roughly 1.3-1.4m matches real proportions. For the low-poly aesthetic I'm considering using 10-sided circular cross-sections with flat (non-smooth) shading to keep the faceted look.

Writing skin paint shader...

Checking texel density against surface area, I settle on 2048 paint size with a 4096 atlas as a reasonable balance of quality and texture budget. For dust accumulation, I'm blending in a muddy color on lower body regions and upward-facing surfaces to mimic elephants throwing dust on their backs.

Darker belly and inner legs where normals point downward, plus darker ground-contact mud near the feet. For the trunk I'm painting ring grooves using the trunk's parametric coordinate, with a lighter pinkish underside, supplemented by torus-shaped relief rings (around 18) for physical detail. Head paint reuses the skin shader with added forehead wrinkles, and I'm planning two SVG textures: an eye decal with lids and wrinkles, and a bristle hair card.

For the remaining textures I'm thinking of reusing the bristle card at larger scale for tail tufts, keeping ears as painted detail rather than a separate decal, and adding two wrinkle decals — curved crease arcs for knees/elbows and concentric brow lines for the forehead/cheeks — applied as dark semi-transparent strokes over the relevant body regions. Ear veins and mud splatter can just be handled through paint rather than extra decals, and tusk wear likewise stays in the paint layer.

Now I'm sketching the eye decal itself: a small ellipse sclera in dark brown, an amber iris, a black pupil, a white highlight, and lash arcs, with wrinkled lid strokes drawn around it, sized small relative to the head. For placement, I need to compute the correct surface hit point and orientation on the head loft near the side-front of the skull, using an angular offset from the head center so the decal sits naturally on the eye socket with proper facing direction.

Working out head geometry next: I'm computing the loft stations to find the head's top height matches the shoulder height, and planning forehead bumps as two domed spheres near the top, skipping cheek bulges and temple depressions for now while adding a brow ridge wedge, and figuring out where the trunk base emerges from the front of the head.

Now I'm plotting the trunk's curve path from base to tip using a chain of points sweeping forward and down then curling slightly upward near the ground, checking radii so nothing clips below the floor, and widening the trunk base to nearly match the head's front width with a smooth bulge.

I'm defining the trunk segments as a named chain for the skeleton (trunk1 through trunk6) parented to the head, with a tapering radius function from base to tip, then adding two small finger-like spikes at the tip to suggest the upper and lower trunk lip.

Now I'm placing the nostril detail at the trunk's tip end — dark flattened sphere shapes scaled into small ellipses, positioned on either side of the tip cap to read as two nostril openings.

Moving on to the chin and lower jaw: I'll set a jaw joint under the head, aimed forward and down, and start building the jaw part.

Working out tusk positions flanking the trunk base, checking overlap with the trunk's radius so they emerge visibly on either side rather than being swallowed by it.

Tapering the tusk radius from base to tip, with the base extending inside the head for a solid join. I'm giving the ivory a gradient paint, shifting from a pale base tone to a worn tip color based on the surface parameter.

For the ears, I'm keeping both faces the same color for simplicity, and maybe adding a slightly pinker inner tone for the earlobe vessels. Eyes get a simple lash treatment or skip them, and I'll add a small flattened brow ridge above each eye.

Hair bristles will be a few curved dark stroke cards placed on the head, chin, and back. For the tail, I'm sweeping a tapered chain about 1.7 meters long down to around y=0.9, finishing with a ring of small black spikes around the tip as a tuft.

I'm thickening that tuft with larger bristle-texture cards plus extra spikes for a signature look, then moving to the feet: deciding on 4 front toenails and 3 hind toenails for an African elephant, building tapered cylinder foot shapes with flat tops, and adding a loose skin-fold ridge at the ankle using a thin torus. Feet rest flush at y=0, and I'm tallying joint counts across the spine, neck, head, jaw, and trunk segments.

Now I'm adding the remaining joints for ears, legs, and tail to get a full skeleton count, noting tusks stay rigid with no joints. I'm working out leg geometry so feet touch the ground properly, then calculating hind leg bend amounts from hip-to-target distances and segment lengths, adjusting the lengths slightly so the knee bend looks natural rather than exaggerated, before moving on to the front leg hip placement.

I'm checking that front leg bend is minimal since elephant front legs appear mostly straight, and adjusting leg radius near the hip so it doesn't bulge too far past the body width. Now I'm thinking through adding wrinkle decals at the knees and ankles using curved crease textures mapped onto the leg surface sweep.

I also want to add temporal gland streaks beneath the eyes, like real African elephants have — a dark teardrop-shaped streak in brown painted into the eye decal below the eye itself, keeping the texture symmetric so mirroring across the body isn't an issue.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for vector creation and mirroring parts across the left/right axis, using a sign convention where positive X is the left side, and checking the API details for sticks, decals, and hit properties before writing the geometry.

Importing the builder, frame, and aiming utilities, then defining RNG, lerp, and path helpers alongside a color palette for skin tones, dust, and mud. Setting up the base color constants...

Still writing wrinkle function...

Still writing skin paint shader...

Still writing ear paint shader...

For the trunk, I'm thinking through ring patterns along its arclength—using sine waves tied to a ~26-ring count over the trunk's length to create periodic darker creases, with the underside lighter grey-pink and the tip shifting to a brighter pink tone.

I want to add mud/dust accumulating toward the trunk's lower tip, so I'll generalize my skin-mixing function to accept an optional ring parameter—when present, it carves creases from one coordinate and lightens the belly using another, blending colors with a simple mix function on Rgb values.

Now I'm scaling a base color by a shading factor and returning it as a tuple, then moving into the builder code—setting up the hips joint as the root spine joint, and building out the spine chain with a Catmull-Rom curve through four points to create three connected spine segments.

Next I'm working out the neck and head joints: the neck chain continues from the spine's last joint through two more points, producing two neck segments, and then I attach a head joint to the final neck segment, checking that its position and direction align properly with the neck's endpoint and that the head's loft geometry sits correctly relative to that joint.

I'm now adding a jaw joint attached to the head with a hinge rotation, then starting to build a reusable leg function that takes a hip root position, foot target, and segment lengths to generate a hip-knee-foot joint chain for each limb.

For the leg mesh, I'm sweeping along each chain with varying radii, leaning toward faceted shading with around 9 sides rather than smooth skinning for a low-poly look, and positioning the foot cylinder near the ground to cap off the leg.

I realize the dome cap at the leg's end would extend below ground level, so I need to raise the leg's end point higher and size the foot cylinder to contain that cap properly, then align the chain tip with the foot part's bone position.

Checking real elephant proportions for the leg and foot thickness, I settle on tapering leg radii from thick at the top (.40) down to thinner at the ankle (.26-.29) before the foot cylinder, which I set at radius .31 to feel appropriately chunky and stylized.

Now I'm figuring out toenail placement -- positioning small flattened spheres as nails around the foot in a ring, oriented outward and spaced symmetrically, with compact dimensions like a short width and slight protrusion so they sit naturally against the foot's surface.

To avoid ambiguity I'll just pass the explicit bone in the stick options instead of relying on nearest-bone inference. Then I'm adding an ankle wrinkle ring using a thin torus geometry near the foot.

Now I'm placing a crease decal on the knee front, positioning it toward the +Z side with a forward offset, and thinking through how decal vertices should inherit skinning weights from the underlying surface.

I'm considering whether to pass the sweep directly as a surface target for shoulder and thigh bulges, possibly adding small haunch spheres scaled and positioned at the hip joint, though I may skip this and just evaluate it in preview first. Now I'm setting up the ear joints, mirrored left and right, defining their position and direction relative to the head.

Working through ear orientation math...

African elephant ears flare much wider than I first sketched, so I'm redoing the rest pose to spread them outward about 1.0m with .75m back, adjusting the thickness axis to face more front/back for a readable fan shape viewed head-on. I'm scaling the ear outline width-to-length ratio around 1.2:1.5 and placing the joint at the ear root.

For attachment, I'm positioning the ear root so its top edge lines up near the head's top (around y=3.4) and the tip hangs down to roughly shoulder height (y=1.75), adding a small bulge sphere at the root for cartilage thickness and skipping the rib detail. Now I'm laying out the head loft stations with width/height values at each vertical point along the skull profile.

I'm adding forehead dome bumps and cheek bulges as scaled spheres at symmetric positions, plus a small "crown" bump between the forehead domes, and a lower lip sphere on the jaw. For the trunk, I'm planning to use the `along` function to place torus wrinkle rings at evenly spaced frames along the trunk's chain, using each point's position and tangent direction.

Still writing trunk rings...

Now I'm sketching bristle shapes as small SVG paths, curved strokes scaled up roughly 2x so they render cleanly at 128px card size.

I'm scattering card instances across the head, body, chin, and trunk tip using surface sampling with minimum distance and normal filters so bristles only grow on upward-facing patches, varying their lean and size by body region. I'm also planning a brow wrinkle ridge placed near the eye hit point, using a flattened sphere part offset upward and outward from the eye location on the head loft surface.

Now I'm working out the eye placement using azimuth and elevation from the skull center, picking roughly 75° azimuth so the eye sits slightly forward, then positioning the ear attachment behind it along z. For the eye decal itself, I'm sizing it around .26 so the drawn eye reads at the right scale, deciding whether to mirror it based on sign, and sketching a forehead crease decal aimed with a forward-upward direction vector toward the head.

I'm planning additional wrinkle decals near the trunk base on each side, settling on just two crease types—one at the knee, one on the brow—to keep things manageable, and skipping a mud splash idea. Then I'm laying out the tail as a chain of joints with decreasing radii from root to tip, parenting it to the spine, and sketching a ring of small tuft spikes around the tail's end frame.

For the tail tuft, I'm making the spikes angle outward with a steep tilt so they flare downward along the tail's direction, adding a center spike running along the tangent for emphasis. I'm also deciding to skip extra bristles along the tail itself since belly dust is already handled through the paint pass.

Finally I'm compiling the list of "wow" details to round out the model: tusk bands, ear veins, eyes, wrinkles, trunk rings, dust paint, foot mud patches via paint, a temporal gland streak, and a pink lip ring around the tusks.

Now I'm thinking through the actual code structure, checking the API for joints, chains, and sweep/loft functions, and confirming how bone references, smoothing options, and polyline paths work together for the limb and body construction.

For leg sweeps I'll key the radius array evenly across the chain with smoothing, and apply skin painting with specific seed and weathering values. For the trunk, I'm planning a catmull path with six points giving five spans plus a tip joint, naming them trunk1 through trunk5 and trunkTip, parented to the head.

Now I'm working out the tip fingers: grabbing the trunk's tip point and tangent to orient a dorsal finger spike using the local frame's up direction relative to that tangent.

Placing nostril offsets along the tangent direction feels fiddly, so I'll simplify by just adding both the dorsal finger and two nostril discs directly at the trunk's end cap rather than overthinking the exact offset math.

I'll write the hair as tapered path polygons in dark brown, skipping any color tint options, and start assembling the texture list for the final file.

For extra details I'm considering a mouth or jaw piece, maybe a lower jaw sphere with a pinkish lip and darker inner mouth, though keeping the overall texture count lean.

Adding more mesh details...

I'm typing the sharp-point tuple into the OutlinePoint array and wiring up the import type from the builder module, then setting the ear root position relative to the joint offset with a slight tilt in the extrude direction.

Positioning the ear base so it's sunk slightly inward against the skull side, around x=.38, and adjusting the bone direction vector accordingly. Starting on the skinPaint function with ring parameter support for the trunk coordinates...

Still writing paint logic...
